🔰SHREDVIEW🔰 - From someone who actually plays and finishes the games before reviewing.

NOTE: If you like my work, please check out the rest of my reviews, I put a lot of work in these to offer the best overall description of what you’re up against. Thank you in advance!

🔷 ABOUT THE GAME & LORE 🔷

Quest Hunter is a co-op action RPG / hack-and-slash game where darkness overtakes the land after the sun goes missing while you’re mid-flight on your airship, forcing a crash. You and your partner (if co-op) must explore mysterious lands, dig for treasure, fight monsters, solve puzzles, and restore balance. The story is light and more like a frame to hang the looting and dungeon crawling around. It has lore and NPCs but choices don’t affect the ending much, your path is mostly fixed.

The game is more about exploring, looting, building your gear, and pushing through enemies. The story gives you reasons to go to new zones but don’t expect plot twists and s**t.

🔷 THE GAMEPLAY 🔷

👉 GENERAL:
Chill, boyo, everything is very simple and straightforward. You hack through dungeons, pick up loot, upgrade gear, repeat. It’s a very simple game, it’s not supposed to have you challenged but relaxed and at least somewhat entertained while at it. 

   •	Combat is basic but does its job. You’ll swing, bash, and repeat until the mobs are cleared. No crazy combos or deep mechanics, just enough responsiveness to keep you awake. Pretty cool.

   •	Exploration adds flavor. You’re not just running corridors, you’re digging up hidden stashes, cracking some easy puzzles, finding keys, and finishing side quests (Quesst hunter, duh). It gives you a little more to chew on to keep you engaged.

   •	Co-op is the selling point. It’s fun playing with a friend, taking a break from complexity and enjoying a decent run of therapy. It may happen that progression doesn’t sync right, I’ve seen this in many titles co-op wise, especially when both players are tracking achievements, it’s a sad reality, the problem is it seems to be consistent in re-occurring.

    •	Replayability isn’t its strength. Once you’re done, you’re done. The game doesn’t have the depth or variety to keep you grinding for weeks, but it’s fine for a one-and-done playthrough.

👉 NAVIGATION SYSTEM:
Maps and waypoints are present. You can mark spots and fast-travel between towns or hubs. The layout is dungeon-based, who would’ve guessed: you pick areas, explore them, return, rinse and repeat. It’s not open world but open section, meaning you can explore somewhat freely but in the section that you’re in. If you get lost in this one, you may want to gift the computer/console to that little eager cousin. 

👉 PHYSICS & MECHANICS:
Nothing fancy. Collisions, hit detection, movement, quite standard. Sometimes clunky edges but nothing that breaks the game. Mechanics focus on hit, loot, upgrade, repeat. Falling off edges into the abyss may be a bit too common as an occurrence but you’ll be fine. One of the achievements specifically tasks you with dying a bunch of times. 

👉  GRAPHICS & OPTIMIZATION:
Visually, it’s pleasant. Doesn’t blow your mind, but it’s clean, colorful, decent for its scale. Lighting, effects, environments do their job and it’s honestly really sexy for a game so niche, quite a stylish underdog. Ran perfectly fine on my end; I saw some “stuttering” complaints. What did y’all play this on? Your microwave? Be fair, be truthful and objective in your reviews you lazy sacks of s**t.

👉  ACHIEVEMENTS & COLLECTIBLES:
This is one area where Quest Hunter delivers. The game has 74 achievements and most of them are unlockable in a single playthrough if you follow quests carefully. Dialogue choices matter for a few. Also, some achievements are missable if you choose wrong dialogue or skip quests, you have been warned. 

🔷  CONCLUSION  🔷

Quest Hunter isn’t no masterpiece. It doesn’t do anything special but it does its job well if you’re looking for simple, cooperative dungeon crawling with loot, secrets, and a light story. The co-op mode is fun but flawed in syncing. If you go in wanting deep narrative or ultra replayability then get the f**k out here, man. Again, if you just want a cool likkle loop to chill with a friend, then get the f**k in here, man.

🔷  PROS & CONS 🔷

✔️ PROS:
-	Achievements are numerous but fair and doable.
-	Pleasant graphics and effects.
-	Looting, puzzles, and exploration are satisfying enough.
-	Simple gear progression and build choices give you some agency.
-	Cool CO-OP experience.

❌ CONS:
-	Replay value fades fast.
-	Mechanics are basic; occasionally clunky. 
-	Missable achievements require careful play or guide.
-	Story is weak, choices don’t matter much.

I've played Quest Hunter as a couch co-op short sessions a couple of days back in 2020, maybe for a total of 4-5 hours. Decided to actually play till the end as a solo in 2025 with a bright thought of "this game looked fine". Ooh boy, I wish I haven't got that thought 10 gameplay hours ago.

There is nothing good to say about the game. Maybe only that the sound/visual components are good. Anything outside of that? Horrible.

Combat is extremely dull. You either fight with your weapon and shield by blocking the first attack and hitting in between enemy attacks (provided you've level up your block and have a good shield) or you run around like a fool waiting for your spells to be off cooldown.

There is no dodge mechanics. It's fairly easy to get stuck between enemies and objects with no way of getting out unless you kill someone and maybe will have time to run out. Blocking is one-directional with no way of turning the block angle. Together with poor controls (at least for KBM) you are often times not blocking the enemy unless you've faced the enemy initially. As soon as multiple enemies pile up you are either taking unnecessary damage or running around like a headless chicken.

Enemy variety is mostly for the looks only. They have slightly different attack animations but as long as that's a melee enemy, that's the same fighting pattern.

And then there's final boss or, rather, final straw to it all [spoiler]as it jumps around the arena outside of your reach while you have unlimited monster spawns as soon as you kill any. And all you can do is run around the arena as well hoping for a faster cooldown and poking the boss with a spell or two doing near-zero damage even with maxed spells. Or try and catch him in the only location you can reach and pray that you aren't blocked by regular monsters as that's a dead end with stairs chokepoint that works against you.[/spoiler]

You can upgrade your weapon, shield and armor for better stats. Funny thing that happens soon after is that you find better gear and realise that upgrading is just a waste of resources as it's capped and you will be changing that upgraded gear piece soon. You get smarter and stop upgrading it all.

There's inventory management that has no "transfer all" button for your storage chest so you have to manually transfer items. Your stored items also do not count for upgrades so you have to pick them (ONE BY ONE) again, upgrade/purchase whatever you needed and put it back in the storage (ONE BY ONE).

Another major drawback is how slow everything is. Maps are quite big yet your character is slow. And some puzzles require you to carry items in your hands making you walk twice as slow and oftentimes you will have to walk across almost the entire map back and forth carrying those. That is anything but fun and enjoyable.

And a big middle finger to completionists - not only there are missable achievements which require you to play the game for a second time but DLC also has achievements added meaning that without giving more money to developers (for a poorly made product) you can't have 100%.

-----

[b]To sum up[/b], name of the company behind this game, 2 Zombie games, makes perfect sense as there is no doubting the fact that no brain has been put in work here. Everything that could have been wrong is wrong and any sense of standard quality is tossed straight into the trash can as commonly expected things aren't there.

Absolutely atrocious game that should be avoided even on sale.

Additionally, it could use more storage slots in the storage chest, which IMO should be bigger than the backpack and a little cheaper upgrades to gear and weapons since they are almost disposable in the sense of being under-powered frequently and require too much to upgrade. The game has a few randomly generated dungeons that you can keep going back to so you can obtain more loot for upgrades but there aren't that many and the tile sets get a little stale after a few playthroughs. Простая, но не унылая за счёт разнообразных умений боевая система. Сложность двоякая: с одной стороны иногда враги довольно сильные, так ещё и толпой нападают, а с другой стороны наказание за смерть — вся добыча сбрасывается и нужно лишь вернуться за ней с последней точки сохранения, враги при этом не воскрешаются и не лечатся, это касается и боссов. Абсурдная, но не упоротая, атмосфера, создаваемая своеобразной графикой, диалогами уровня детсада (но таки забавными) и банальным сюжетом об оказавшемся в "нужное" время в "нужном" месте герое, который вынужден помогать всем, чтобы, в конце концов, вернуть пропавшее солнце и попутно для себя лично всё наладить. Куча секретов, раздолье для исследований и гринда, случайные события и опциональные случайно-генерируемые подземелья... Это всё здорово и позволило мне растянуть прохождение сюжета на 13 часов.
Минусы, конечно, есть, такие как музыка, которая не блещет разнообразием в процессе прохождения, и сомнительной полезности системы крафта и улучшения экипировки. Но, не смотря на это, как увеселительная, не слишком мрачная и несерьёзная РПГ Quest Hunter со своей задачей справляется, не вызывая отторжения. Так ещё и в кооперативе до 4 человек играть можно.

Отдельно хочу отметить и поблагодарить разработчиков за то, что не следуют моде на "гендерное разнообразие" и прочую туфту. Играть можно только за персонажа мужского пола, потому что сюжет таков, что игрок отыгрывает роль героя, сильного мужчины, спасителя мира, принцесс и других милых дам, которые восхищаются им не за красивые глазки, а за совершаемые подвиги. Традиционные ценности, ура!

ほとんどのシステムに難あり、やっていても楽しくない。
いいところを上げるとすれば唯一BGMがいいぐらいで、
あとはマイナス。

まず歩行速度が亀なみ、これは中盤、終盤で移動速度アップのスキルやポーションが
作れるようになるが、システム上非常に残念なことにアクティブスキルなので
いちいち掛けなおさないといけない。肝心のスキルはまあまあの数あるのに、
ショートカットキーが三つしかなく、そのうちの一つを移動速度アップに振ってしまうと、
戦闘で使える攻撃スキルが一つ減ることになり、ただでさえテンポの悪い戦闘が余計にテンポ悪くなる。
せめてCTもっと短くするとか、移動速度はパッシブにするとかならまだ救いはあった。
で、物体を運んだりするときに重いのでただでさえ遅い移動速度がさらに遅くなり、
第三章に関しては移動速度大幅ダウン+ダメージの沼地が登場し、プレイヤーのやる気を一気に削ってくる。
ちなみにただでさえうっとうしい沼地フィールドなのに、
出てくる敵が遠距離+そもそも沼地が暗くてよくみえないので、
知らず知らずのうちにダメうけて倒れたりする。

スキルだが上述の通り三つしかショートカットがないのも大問題だが、
なによりスキルの射程や範囲がまったく表示されないのも大問題。
結局このスキルを使ってどこまで届くのか、何を破壊できるのかがわからない。
で、毒が物体を壊せないのはスキルの説明でなんとなく納得はできるが、
ゾンビに毒がきかないなら書いといてほしい。
炎のスキルはなぜかターゲットではなく向いている方向に発動するため、
敵をタゲティングしてても後ろを向いてたら全然意味なく発動してしまう。

ポーションに関して、終盤はかなり多めに使うことになるのに
素材が手に入りにくい。特に赤い花はかなりのレアアイテム。

マルチプレイをすると敵が３倍ぐらい強くなり、
ポーション類がぶ飲み状態なのに、宝箱から出てくるアイテムや素材は
まさかのとったもの勝ち。マルチだからってアイテムや素材の数が倍以上出てくるわけではない。
つまりジリ貧になるのでマルチはおすすめしない、なんならやる意味がない。

最後に、謎解きが分かりにくい。
特に第二章最後のダンジョンの４つのレバーや、３つの玉のところなんて、
何十、何百通りもある中からヒントなしでみつけなければならない。
つまり時間の無駄。どうせならどこかにヒントでも示しておくべき。
もはや謎解きとは言えないレベル。

最後になりましたが、改善する余地しかないゲームなので
大幅にアプデとかして改善されない限りは本当におすすめしません。

The game is BAD..... EDIT: it is also old, AND, only 10% of the players obtained the end game achievement... so, make of that what you will.

The story is a nothing burguer worthy of a cellphone game (which this one is), it is so BAD, it is almost a meme, there is a missing princess and the [spoiler] Sun [/spoiler] has been stolen from the sky, so theres chaos... if you want to know HOW MUCH of a meme story is this, here is a spoiler for you [spoiler] the sun (not a representation, the ACTUAL sun) is being held at the final boss' old house... in its basement, along with the princess [/spoiler] and the motive for it is [spoiler] "just felt like it" as per the final boss' admition...  [/spoiler] yyyyyyyeah, some things are so cringe they hurt, dont they?


The writing of the characters is again, worthy of a cellphone game (which this one is), the only redeeming factor of the characters is the drawing style of their character sheets.

THE GAMEPLAY----------------------------------------------------------

This is a hack n' slash ARPG, but there are no character classes, with a LOT of puzzles (more on that later).
Every time you  level up, you get 3 stats points.  You only get 3 stats which dont do much, they are you HP, which you increase by 5 with every point, your armor (kid you not), every point you put on it makes you absorb a certain percentage of damage, and your shield, every point you put on it makes your shield absorb a certain (absolute, not relative) amount of damge IF you guard with the shield in the direction you are being attacked from (most final maps will have you mobbed, so,  no much use for the shield in those.

You get skills (spells)  too, and they are another nothing burguer, and ONE of them is almost A MUST (unless you ARE on the look for self unaliving reasons). You level up this spells by using loot, you can only equip 3 of these seplls at a time, and leveling them up, only changes their stats, no cool new effects, no epic moves, nothing.

The bosses are all (except for one who has a shortcut) just about running around while waiting for your skills cooldown to be done, get a few hits in, rince a repeat.  no attack patterns to learn, no weaknesses to exploit, nothing

The worst part is the lack of speed for anything,  this game has a LOT of back tracking and the movement between locations is where encouters for grinding occur. later this is fixed, but it takes away the grinding and thus the loot picking to level up your spells slows to a crawl and you cant opt out of this new moving mechanic.  The moving around INSIDE a stage is ALSO slow (unless you spam the speed spell) which is particularly bad when you have to deal with the puzzles.....

THE PUZZLES: most of them are obvious, some of them dont even have hints, they are just try combinations untill you get it right, some are about taking items from one point of the map to the other (that sometimes means crossing the ENTIRE map pushing some kind of object through enemies and traps... kind of an escort mission for a rock... remeber i said the game  is slow... yeah.. not fun.

Theres also a multiplayer option, but its dead and there is some kind of (i guess) map score board game mode with ranking, theres also a DLC which opens more of the map.... not gonna do ANY of that to myself
